# #440 — SEARCH-1: the policy layer (_DOCS, _ob) is in no qmd index — agents cannot find the rules they are judged by

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: enhancement
Created: 2026-07-29T18:22:32Z
Updated: 2026-07-29T18:22:32Z

---

The Development-wide `_DOCS/` and `_ob/` trees — standards, SOPs, canonical skills and procedures — are indexed **nowhere**. Not the repo index, not fleet, not research.

## Measured 2026-07-29

```
fleet.sqlite: 10,900 documents, 40+ collections
  documents from _DOCS: 0
  documents from _ob:   0
```

The `open-brain` repo collection covers this repo's own `docs/`, `_DOCS/`, and `_plans/` — that part is fine. The gap is everything above the repo root.

## Consequences, both observed this session

1. **`_DOCS/QMD_INDEXES.md` exists and is complete** (150 lines: the general form `ROOT=/some/tree INDEX=othername qmd-reference-index`, the naming standard, the live `research` example). An `ai-agents` session needed it, could not find it, improvised with `qmd-backfill` on a third-party checkout, and committed an index allowlist into `github.com/block/buzz`. The tool's own header warns against exactly that.
2. **`_ob/skills/skill-maintainer/workflows/update.md` exists** and says an edit made in a runtime adapter is a fork, not an update. Unreachable by search; this session forked the `brain` skill anyway.

The policy layer that governs how every agent works is the only body of knowledge not searchable, so agents reliably fail in the ways it warns about.

## Scope

- A named `policy` index over `_DOCS` + `_ob`, using the existing parameterized builder: `ROOT=... INDEX=policy qmd-reference-index`.
- Route it so ordinary agent searches reach it (`aqmd` currently scopes to THIS repo by design and never the fleet).
- Do **not** solve this by widening the repo index — the scoping guard exists because unscoped runs cost a GPU hour (2026-07-27).

## Note on layering

This is the *retrieval* half only. The always-known half is #438/#439: canon carries the short absolute rule, the index serves the full procedure on trigger. Index-only is what failed here — an agent that does not know a rule exists never searches for it.

Design: `_plans/canon-always-known.md`
